questions.q: In Microsoft Sentinel, which two pieces together make up the practical SOAR stack this chapter builds?
options: An Automation Rule and a Logic App playbook
A KQL analytics rule and a workbook
A hunting query and a watchlist
An entity and an analytics rule template
questions.explain: An Automation Rule watches for incidents matching a condition and decides what to trigger; a Logic App playbook is the actual workflow of connector actions it runs.

questions.q: Which of these is a realistic, well-suited use of SOAR automation according to this lesson?
options: Deciding, without a defined rule, whether an ambiguous alert is a false positive
Judging whether disabling a specific VIP's account right now is proportionate
Posting a standardized comment and pulling context into an incident the moment it opens
Weighing a conflicting signal like a change-ticket against an unusual sign-in location
questions.explain: Posting a standard comment and pulling context is high-volume and fully deterministic -- exactly what SOAR automation is good at. The other options all require judgment a workflow engine doesn't have.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a playbook that auto-closes 'low severity, single failed sign-in' incidents is risky?
options: Because Logic Apps cannot process severity fields at all
Because it will keep closing them unchanged even during a real password-spray campaign, since nothing tells it circumstances changed
Because Sentinel does not allow automation rules to act on severity
Because closing incidents automatically is against Microsoft's terms of service
questions.explain: A playbook executes exactly the condition it was given, including when that condition is wrong for current circumstances -- it has no awareness that the situation around it has changed.

questions.q: What does the 'orchestration' part of SOAR refer to?
options: Running a Python script with no human review
The approval gate placed in front of containment actions
The KQL query language used inside analytics rules
Connecting separate tools like the SIEM, identity provider, EDR, and chat into one workflow instead of manual console-switching
questions.explain: Orchestration is the wiring that lets systems like Sentinel, Microsoft Entra ID, Defender for Endpoint, and Teams pass data to each other through one workflow engine.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the realistic end-to-end shape of SOAR that this chapter builds toward?
options: Automate the pipeline (enrichment, orchestration) and gate any action with real blast radius behind human approval
A fully autonomous system that decides and executes containment with no human involved
Replace the SOC analyst role entirely with scripted decision rules
Use SOAR only for closing alerts, never for enrichment or containment
questions.explain: The chapter's realistic and defensible shape is: automate the deterministic pipeline work, and stop at a human approval gate before any action with real blast radius executes.
